description: Use CA-generated bent or semi-bent Boolean functions as spectral templates for length-167 block candidates. The CA does not try to output an order-668 Hadamard directly; it supplies Walsh-flat shadows that are decoded into candidates likely to survive modular or exact filters.
mathematical_formalization: For a CA rule r and seed s, derive a Boolean function f_{r,s}. Compute Walsh profile W_f(omega) = sum_x (-1)^(f(x) + omega.x). Project spectrally flat signatures through a map Pi into candidate block tuples (a,b,c,d) and score them by autocorrelation debt J(Pi(f)).
analogical_connections: CA rule evolution as a Fourier-prior generator.
Shadow decoding from spectral space into sequence space.
implementation_hypothesis: Search over CA rules already known to yield bent-like functions, define one or more projection maps into 167-length binary blocks, and keep only shadows enriched for modular admissibility.
experiment_seed: Measure enrichment against random supports and direct local search on smaller targets before applying the same decoder to 167-length blocks.

closest_prior_art.title: Heuristic Search of (Semi-)Bent Functions based on Cellular Automata

novelty_claim: The new step is a target-specific decoder from CA-generated spectral objects into the exact obstruction space for order 668.
differentiation: Prior CA-bent papers optimize cryptographic quality in their own right. Here spectral flatness is only a proposal prior and success is judged by Hadamard-specific filters.
